evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解 / 字形 / 《說文》 / 《廣韻》
evidence.text: The database reports the bronze graph 飯 as 食 plus 反, with 反 functioning as phonetic. It quotes the Shuowen definition 食也，从食反聲 and two Guangyun spellings, 扶晚 and 符万. Its explanation, following Duan Yucai, takes the early verbal sense as ‘eat’ and the noun sense ‘what is eaten’ or cooked rice as an extension. A bronze inscription has 飯者月 as a Qi month name, but the database says which month it denotes is unknown. The page displays one bronze example and one Small Seal example; its text alone does not establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 飯

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis 飯，食也。从食，反聲, and its fanqie 符萬切. The page distinguishes the graph’s structure from the semantic account: it reports 食 as the semantic component and 反 as the phonetic component.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 飯

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting Duan Yucai’s 說文解字注
evidence.text: Duan interprets 飯’s 食 sense as the action ‘to eat’ and says it extended to the thing eaten. He also cautions that the modern tonal distinction between 食 and 飯 was not present in the same way in ancient usage. This is a Qing commentator’s historical interpretation, not a dated attestation of the semantic change.
evidence.title: 說文解字「食」— Shuowen.org

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, dictionary and Analects text
evidence.field: 引用古籍 / 論語·述而
evidence.text: The dictionary page quotes the Analects phrase 飯疏食飲水, where 飯 is verbal (‘eat’) and 疏食 is coarse/simple food. This supplies an early literary use of 飯 as a verb; the web page gives no independent date for the passage’s composition, so it should not be treated as a precisely dated first occurrence.
evidence.title: 飯 — 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 字音 / 中古音 / 形義通解
evidence.text: For 飯 the page gives Mandarin fàn in its headword display and shows Guangyun fanqie 扶晚 and 符万, corresponding to two readings with voiced labial initials, rising and departing categories. For 反 it gives Mandarin fǎn and Guangyun entries 孚袁 and 府遠, with aspirated and voiceless labial initials in the listed categories. Modern same-syllable similarity alone does not prove the phonetic history; the medieval categories and Old Chinese reconstructions provide historical comparison.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 飯

evidence.source: Wiktionary, citing Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction 1.1 (2014)
evidence.text: In the Baxter–Sagart system as reported on the page, 飯 has readings reconstructed *bonʔ ‘eat’ and *bonʔ-s ‘cooked rice or millet’; 反 has *Cə.panʔ ‘reverse’ (and a separate reading). These reconstructions have related labial onset and nasal-final/rhyme material but do not make 反 and 飯 identical in every feature. They support a plausible phonetic relationship in the compound rather than a claim that 飯 is a whole-graph loan from 反. The page also lists Zhengzhang’s reconstruction for 反 as *panʔ; that is a different system and is not directly interchangeable with Baxter–Sagart.
evidence.title: Appendix:Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 《說文》 / 形義通解 / 中古音
evidence.text: The 反 entry quotes Shuowen 覆也，从又、厂 and reports bronze, oracle-bone and seal-script forms in its glyph section. Its explanation presents a scholarly interpretation of the early forms as a hand (又) at a cliff-like form (厂 or 石), interpreted by Yang Shuda as a person climbing or clinging to a cliff; it presents ‘turn/reverse’ as an extended sense. The page also reports 反 being used in bronze inscriptions for 返, but that is whole-graph usage of 反 in another word and is distinct from 反’s phonetic role inside 飯.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 反

evidence.text: The database’s text identifies bronze inscription 集成04140 and describes 反’s original meaning as turning the palm over, with 又 ‘hand’ as semantic element and 厂 as phonetic element. This is a source assertion about 反 itself; it does not establish the object or name of any depicted tool, nor is such a tool hypothesis needed to analyze 反 as the phonetic element in 飯.
evidence.title: 漢字「反」：字形演變

evidence.field: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议
evidence.text: The ministry-hosted decision says the first table of the simplification scheme was to be used from 1 February 1956. This establishes the scheme’s implementation date but the inspected page excerpt does not show the specific 饭 entry; therefore it does not alone document the character-specific derivation 饭 from 飯 or the history of the food radical’s abbreviated shape.
evidence.title: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议(1956年)

gaps: The CUHK entry reports only one bronze 飯 example, “飯者月,” and explicitly leaves the month identity unknown; no securely dated earliest occurrence or clear food-related context for that bronze use was established.

The received Shuowen entry is an early Han dictionary witness, but this research did not establish the earliest independent attestation of the verbal ‘eat’ sense or the noun sense ‘cooked rice/food’. Analects examples are transmitted textual evidence without a precise composition date here.

The semantic transition from ‘eat’ (verb) to ‘what is eaten’ and then ‘cooked rice/meal’ is reported by Duan Yucai/CUHK; this research did not establish dated intermediate attestations or a more detailed chronology.

No visually inspected glyph images or primary inscription facsimiles were obtained for 飯, so graphic development beyond the database’s report of bronze 飯 and a Small Seal form cannot be independently described. The character-specific simplified-form history 饭 and the origin of 饣 require a direct inspected historical orthography source; the official decision page opened here only supports the general scheme timing.

For 飯 as a graphic compound, 反 is independently supported as phonetic by Shuowen and the bronze analysis, with modern Mandarin fàn/fǎn, Cantonese Jyutping faan6/faan2 (CUHK’s tone notation), medieval Guangyun fanqie, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms documented. The exact historical sound change or phonological motivation behind the component’s use remains unresolved by the inspected sources.

The early pictorial interpretation of 反 is disputed at the level of referent: CUHK relays a cliff-climbing interpretation, whereas the Academia Sinica database reports a turned-palm analysis and treats 厂 as phonetic. These should remain competing source analyses, not a settled depiction.

The imported Wiktionary note about Mon-Khmer cooked-rice comparison and the claim about English fan as a separate loan usage were not externally investigated here; neither is needed to explain 飯’s graphic formation.

The bronze-style SVG is a candidate modern drawing, not an artifact photograph. Because its description page could not be opened and a Commons file page was not found, its source image, authorship details, and reuse license were not verified to the required standard.
No character-specific Xiaoxuetang record, exact rendered-glyph URL, or official CC0 notice was inspected. No Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.

No historical glyph image is selected: identity and reuse provenance remain unverified. Dossier evidence reports a bronze 飯 form and a Small Seal form, but no candidate image from those sources was visually inspected here.
